defaults.permitted_development: Across Surrey, a temporary building is not exempt simply because it will be removed later. The planning answer usually turns on how fixed it is, how long it remains, what it is used for and whether any specific temporary-use right actually applies.

rules.height_rules: There is no standard height allowance for temporary buildings. The taller and more engineered the structure looks, the harder it is to present it as a minor temporary feature rather than operational development needing permission.
rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. Footprint, duration, services, foundations and the intensity of use matter far more than one single measurement.
rules.boundary_rules: Across Surrey, access, traffic, noise, overlooking, servicing and visibility at the site edge are often what turn a supposedly temporary structure into a proposal that needs fuller planning scrutiny.
rules.roof_rules: A fixed or heavily engineered roof can quickly make a temporary structure look permanent. Wind loading, rainwater handling and visual bulk all matter.
rules.materials_rules: Use reversible, low-glare materials and temporary-looking details. Heavy cladding, permanent foundations and hard-wired services tend to undermine the temporary case.

rules.permitted_development: The word temporary does not settle the planning position. What matters is how long the structure remains, how fixed it is and what activity it supports. In Elmbridge, the temporary case usually weakens when the structure starts to look permanent in both appearance and day-to-day use.

rules.height_rules: Height for a temporary building is judged through bulk, visibility and whether the structure still reads as genuinely short-term rather than semi-permanent. rules.depth_rules: There is no standard depth rule. Footprint, duration, services, foundations and the overall intensity of use matter much more than one single measurement.
rules.boundary_rules: At the boundary, temporary structures are often judged by how they behave: access, queues, deliveries, lighting and neighbour impact. In Elmbridge, the site edge is usually tested by how much openness and domestic breathing room the temporary structure takes away.
rules.roof_rules: A fixed or fully engineered roof can push a proposal toward being treated as a building rather than a lightweight temporary structure. Wind resistance, rainwater disposal and visual bulk all matter.
rules.materials_rules: Use reversible, low-glare materials and details that support the temporary case. Heavy cladding, permanent foundations and utility connections make the structure harder to describe as temporary. The more fixed, serviced and visually dominant the structure becomes, the harder it is to rely on a temporary argument.

restrictions.conservation_area: Even short-term structures can be difficult in a conservation area if they add visual clutter or interrupt an established historic scene.
restrictions.listed_building: Temporary works affecting a listed building, its curtilage or its setting can still need listed building consent and separate planning review.
restrictions.article4_notes: Even short-term structures can lose the easier planning route where an Article 4 direction removes the normal fallback for that site.
